commitResults.messageTitle: Level-0: Rename chatbot to Nova, add greet and exit
Level-1: Echo input, exit on bye
Level-3: Mark tasks as done and unmark
Level-5: Handle invalid user input gracefully
A-Enums: Model task status as an enum
Add save and load support for tasks
Save tasks whenever the task list changes
Use LocalDate for deadline and event dates
Organize code into the nova package
Add JUnit tests for core classes
Add Javadoc comments to all public classes
Follow Java coding standard for layouts
Add find command to search tasks

commitResults.messageBody:
# Conflicts:
#	src/main/java/nova/Ui.java

commitResults.messageTitle: Use varargs for Ui message printing
commitResults.messageBody:
Add showMessage(String... messages) that prints each message on its own
line and route greet, bye, add/delete/status confirmations and errors
through it, replacing repeated System.out.println calls.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Checkstyle to the Gradle build
commitResults.messageBody:
Use the SE-EDU checkstyle.xml and suppressions.xml from AddressBook
Level 3 (config/checkstyle/) with checkstyle tool version 11.0.0.

Fix the reported violations: add missing Javadoc to Storage#save and
Storage#load, and ensure every Java file ends with a newline.

Follow the SE-EDU JavaFX tutorial (parts 1-4): JavaFX 17.0.7
dependencies in build.gradle, Launcher + Main application entry,
MainWindow and DialogBox controllers with FXML views, and avatar
images. Nova now exposes getResponse(String) so the text-based UI and
the GUI share the same command logic; the text UI is kept for easy
testing and the bye command is retained. mainClass now points at
nova.Launcher.

commitResults.messageTitle: Polish the GUI: window title, greeting and bye exit
commitResults.messageBody:
Set the stage title to Nova, show a greeting dialog and focus the input
field on startup, and make the bye command close the application via
Platform.exit (the FXML controller is not the root node, so it cannot
use getScene()). Nova#isExitCommand is shared by the text loop and the
GUI.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename vague identifiers per peer review

commitResults.messageBody: A-Assertions: document assumptions with assertions

Mark, unmark and delete repeat the same task-number parsing and error
handling. Centralizing it in one helper removes the triplication and
gives later commands a single place to reuse.

No behavior change; all existing tests still pass.
A-CodeQuality: extract command helpers in Nova

commitResults.messageTitle: Express find and list formatting with streams

commitResults.messageBody: A-Streams: use streams for find and list formatting

commitResults.messageTitle: Add archive command for completed tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Completed tasks clutter the list once done. The archive command moves
them to data/nova-archive.txt and removes them from the list, keeping
a record in the same save format.

Usage: archive (no arguments). Reports the archived tasks, or a message
when there is nothing completed to archive.
C-Archive: add archive command for completed tasks

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract command parsing and harden error handling
commitResults.messageBody:
Nova.executeCommand split the raw input itself and every command
repeated the same whitespace, duplicate-parameter and range checks, so
bad input produced either a vague reply or no reply at all.

Let's pull the split into a Parser and report every error we can name:
repeated /by, /from or /to labels, an event that ends before it starts,
extra arguments on commands that take none, and a save file that cannot
be read or written.

Parsing is now testable on its own, which the new ParserTest covers.
A-MoreErrorHandling: extract Parser and report input errors

commitResults.messageTitle: Show errors and replies differently in the GUI
commitResults.messageBody:
Every reply looked identical in the chat, so an error such as a bad
date was as easy to miss as a successful add.

Let's return a CommandResult carrying the text and the kind of reply
from executeCommand, and style each dialog box by kind, and drop the
pixel coordinates in MainWindow.fxml so the window can be resized
without the input bar drifting away from the bottom edge.

commitResults.messageTitle: Polish the chat window and make it themeable
commitResults.messageBody:
The chat worked but read as a text area: no timestamps, no sense of
which reply changed something, no way to see how many tasks there are,
and no way to find a command you have forgotten.

Let's give the window a header with the product name, a live task count
and a theme switch, put a tail, a timestamp and a kind marker on every
bubble, and remember the theme and the window position between runs.

Nova also answers help, the input field recalls earlier commands with
the up and down arrows and completes a command word with Tab, and the
palette lives in one stylesheet with light and dark values.
A-BetterGui: distinguish errors and polish the chat window

commitResults.messageTitle: Give Nova one consistent voice in every reply
commitResults.messageBody:
The replies mixed flat confirmations ("Ok", "Noted", "Got it") with
technical messages, and the count sentence read "1 tasks".

Let's settle on Nova's voice: a short, warm acknowledgement that names
what just happened, singular and plural counts handled properly, and
error messages that say what to type instead.

The window's palette, name and avatar already match this personality;
this commit is the wording.
A-Personality: a consistent voice for Nova

commitResults.messageTitle: Test the command surface, history and storage
commitResults.messageBody:
Only the task, list and storage classes had tests, so the command
handling that carries most of the behaviour was checked by hand.

Let's drive Nova through a storage injected into a temporary folder and
assert the reply for every command: add, mark, unmark, delete, find,
archive, help, bye, the invalid inputs, and the singular and plural
wording. Storage gains tests for the error paths it reports, and
CommandHistory gains tests for the arrow-key behaviour.
A-MoreTesting: JUnit coverage for the command surface

commitResults.messageTitle: Credit reused work, fix the product name and dates
commitResults.messageBody:
The project README still showed the template's mascot art and pointed at a
task class that has since moved into a package, and nothing named the
libraries the project depends on, which the reuse policy asks for.

Let's acknowledge the libraries and the reused starting point in the
README, replace the sample output with Nova's own banner, pin the date
format to English so every machine prints the same dates, and record
the reused work in CONTRIBUTORS.md.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add the user guide and product screenshot
commitResults.messageBody:
docs/README.md was still the template with placeholder comments, so the
product website would have published empty instructions.

Let's write the user guide for Nova itself: every command with an
example and the reply to expect, quick start, where tasks are saved and
the errors a user may see, plus docs/Ui.png showing the full window.

GitHub Pages serves the docs folder, so the guide becomes the product
website.
